requirements.evidence: Contract matches: CallMode enum with the three backed cases (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the specified signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:28). Queue row is locked and is_active re-read from DB (:33-40); ordering priority desc, issued_at, id (:90-94); normal_only oldest first (:81-84); priority_only filter (:91); fairness via last 3 calls ordered by called_at desc, id desc (:104-116) with fallback to ordered when no normal waits (:97); candidate is locked and re-checked, skipped ids excluded (:45-57); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set and the locked model returned (:59-64); NoWaitingTicketsException when nothing is eligible (:67). Both docs updated. Small robustness concern: the history filters on status = called (:108), so it would miss tickets that later move to another status.

conventions.evidence: The domain write sits in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php as a single use-case class, with no service or repository layer. A Pest feature test ships with it (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php). docs/business-rules.md, docs/architecture.md ("Call the next ticket") and CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] are updated, and the public method has PHPDoc with @throws. There is no authorization in the action, which the task explicitly asks for.

security.evidence: No HTTP or Livewire surface and authorization is out of scope per the task. Writes use explicit attribute assignment, not mass assignment (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:59-62). Concurrency is handled with lockForUpdate on the queue (:33-36) and on the candidate (:46-49) inside DB::transaction, and the status is re-checked, so the same ticket cannot be called twice. The passed queue model is not trusted. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: 13 tests cover ordering and the id tie-break (test:39-48), the returned and persisted fields (:50-63), other queues and already-called tickets (:65-74), an empty queue (:76), an inactive stale queue with nothing changed (:80-88), priority_only and normal_only including their exceptions (:90-112), fairness trigger, no-normal fallback and fewer-than-3 cases (:114-136, :171-178), and a simulated concurrent call via a retrieved hook (:180-202). Gaps: the test named 'a normal_only call resets the streak' (:138) actually makes the normal call in Any mode, and the 'called_at then id' test (:160) uses distinct called_at values, so the id tie-break in history is not exercised.

simplicity.evidence: The action is about 115 lines. Small query closures ($waiting, $normals, $ordered) are reused instead of copy-pasted queries (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:76-94), there is a single named constant FAIRNESS_STREAK, and there is no extra abstraction. Builder->when() is used for the priority_only filter.

readability.evidence: Clear names (pick, priorityStreakReached, $lockedQueue, $skipped), short focused methods, and useful comments on why the queue is re-read and why candidates are re-locked (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:31-32, :42-44). There is no dead code or debug output. The test helpers waiting() and called() keep the tests readable.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only the action, enum, exception, its test, the two docs the task requires, and the CHANGELOG entry that conventions.md requires. There are no unrelated edits.

issues.explanation: The test title says a normal_only call resets the streak, but the normal call at :153 uses the default Any mode, so neither 'normal_only calls count in history' nor 'a normal_only call resets the streak' is actually tested.
The test 'uses called_at then id to find the last three calls' gives every row a distinct called_at, so the id desc tie-break in the fairness history is never exercised.

Fairness history selects only tickets whose status is still 'called'. If a called ticket later moves to another status (served, finished and so on), it drops out of the 'last 3 called' window. Filtering on called_at IS NOT NULL would be more robust.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action with the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException. It implements deterministic ordering, the three modes, the 3-priority-calls fairness rule, the inactive-queue check under lock, and exactly-once calling by locking and re-checking the candidate, with docs and CHANGELOG updated. The code is lean, correct and well tested. The only gaps are two slightly mislabeled or incomplete fairness tests and a history query that depends on the ticket still being in the 'called' status, so I would approve with minor follow-ups.
